description: Portable human checkpoint policy — defines autonomous vs approval-required actions across all runtimes

autonomous.description: Actions the agent may perform autonomously within task contracts
actions: Read any file in the repository
Edit source code files within the assigned task contract
Create new source code, test, and documentation files
Run formatters, linters, typecheckers, and safe local tests
Create feature branches and isolated git worktrees
Update state files (.ai/state/) and project telemetry
Install dependencies specified in task requirements
Run local development test fixtures or seeders
Create or modify environment template files (.env.example)

askUserBefore.description: Actions requiring explicit user authorization before execution

actions.action: Destructive database actions (DROP, TRUNCATE, raw migrations on live databases)
Production deployment and cloud provisioning (terraform apply, cdk deploy)
Displaying, committing, or modifying live secrets and credentials
Destructive filesystem operations (rm -rf /, format, git clean -fdx)
Payment and billing transaction processing logic modifications
Breaking public API contract changes without backward-compatibility deprecation
Package publishing or public release artifact generation

enforcement.deterministicHooks: If supported by the runtime (e.g. Antigravity PreToolUse, Cursor/Copilot confirmation, Claude Code permissions), wire deterministic interceptors.
enforcement.agentGuard: Main agent and subagents must check commands against this policy before dispatching.
